title: Social media, looksmaxxing, and why men struggle with body image, with Roberto Olivardia, PhD

sentences.en: Young men today receive a lot of messages about how they should look.
sentences.zh: 如今的年轻男性接收到大量关于自己外表应该如何的讯息。

sentences.en: Scroll through social media and you'll find influencers peddling advice on building muscle, losing body fat, improving your jawline, and maximizing your attractiveness.
sentences.zh: 浏览社交媒体，你会发现到处都是网红在兜售关于如何增肌、减脂、塑造完美下颌线以及最大化个人魅力的建议。

sentences.en: Entire online communities exist around the idea that a male's appearance can and should be constantly improved.
sentences.zh: 整个网络社群都建立在一个观念之上：男性的外表可以而且应该不断得到改善。

sentences.en: What are these messages doing to men and boys?
sentences.zh: 这些讯息对广大男性和男孩们产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: For years, body image concerns were seen as something that primarily affected women and girls.
sentences.zh: 多年来，身材焦虑主要被视为困扰女性和女孩的问题。

sentences.en: But today, there's increasing recognition that boys and men also struggle with body dissatisfaction and eating disorders, and that social media might be making the problem worse.
sentences.zh: 但如今，人们越来越认识到，男孩和男性同样也在遭受身材不满和饮食失调的困扰，而社交媒体可能正在使这一问题愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: So how common are body image concerns among boys and men?
sentences.zh: 那么，身材焦虑在男孩和男性中究竟有多普遍？

sentences.en: In what ways do eating disorders and body dysmorphic disorders in men look different than they look in women and girls?
sentences.zh: 男性和男孩的饮食失调以及身体变形障碍，与女性和女孩的表现有哪些不同？

sentences.en: Why do they so often go unrecognized?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们常常不被察觉？

sentences.en: What role is social media playing in shaping men's perceptions of their bodies?
sentences.zh: 社交媒体在塑造男性对其身材的认知方面发挥了什么作用？

sentences.en: And what can parents, clinicians, and others do to help boys and men develop a healthy relationship with their appearance?
sentences.zh: 父母、临床医生以及其他人可以做些什么来帮助男孩和男性建立健康的体貌认知？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客节目，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Roberto Olivardia, a clinical psychologist at McLean Hospital in Boston and a lecturer in psychology at Harvard Medical School.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是罗伯托·奥利瓦迪亚博士，他是波士顿麦克莱恩医院的临床心理学家，也是哈佛医学院的心理学讲师。

sentences.en: He and his colleagues coined the term muscle dysmorphia nearly 30 years ago as a subtype of body dysmorphic disorder that primarily affects men.
sentences.zh: 他和同事在近 30 年前创造了“肌肉异形症”一词，将其作为主要影响男性的身体变形障碍的一个亚型。

sentences.en: Today, he specializes in the treatment of body dysmorphic disorder and eating disorders, as well as ADHD and obsessive compulsive disorder.
sentences.zh: 如今，他专门从事身体变形障碍、饮食失调以及多动症和强迫症的治疗。

sentences.en: He is a co-author of the book, The Adonis Complex, The Secret Crisis of Male Body Obsession, and he's spoken widely to the media about issues related to body image in boys and men.
sentences.zh: 他是《阿多尼斯综合征：男性体貌执念的秘密危机》一书的合著者，并就男孩和男性的身材焦虑相关问题接受过各大媒体的广泛采访。

sentences.en: Dr. Olivardia, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 奥利瓦迪亚博士，非常感谢您今天作客本节目。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 非常荣幸。

sentences.en: Well, let's start with the big picture.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们从宏观层面开始聊起。

sentences.en: I mentioned in the introduction that body image is often viewed as a concern primarily for girls and women.
sentences.zh: 我在介绍中提到，身材焦虑通常被认为是主要困扰女孩和女性的问题。

sentences.en: Why is that and how has our understanding of body image concerns in boys and men changed over the past few decades?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？在过去几十年里，我们对男孩和男性身材焦虑的理解发生了怎样的变化？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So contrary to what people believe is that 25% of people who have eating disorders are boys and men.
sentences.zh: 与人们所认为的相反，患有饮食失调的人群中有 25% 是男孩和男性。

sentences.en: Now, many years ago, when I started entering into this research arena, we didn't see that epidemiological data.
sentences.zh: 然而很多年前，当我刚开始进入这个研究领域时，我们并没有看到这样的流行病学数据。

sentences.en: And part of it was, A, there weren't a lot of studies looking at boys and men, or the assessment measures were not really valid or reliable for male populations.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，首先，当时没有很多针对男孩和男性的研究，或者评估工具对男性群体来说并不真正有效或可靠。

sentences.en: Boys and men were not presenting clinically.
sentences.zh: 男孩和男性当时并未到临床就诊。

sentences.en: And so it was difficult in terms of getting research because a lot of research on boys and men were just being, in the early 90s, were being drawn from just clinical samples, which
sentences.zh: 因此在获取研究数据方面存在困难，因为在 90 年代初期，对男孩和男性的许多研究仅仅取材于临床样本，

sentences.en: represented just a slice of the boys and men who were struggling.
sentences.zh: 而这些样本只能代表苦苦挣扎的男孩和男性中的一小部分。

sentences.en: So we know that it's much more common than people think it is.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，这种情况比人们想象的要普遍得多。

sentences.en: And having done this work for over 30 years, I've seen just increased awareness.
sentences.zh: 而且我从事这项工作已经 30 多年了，我亲眼看到公众意识的不断提高。

sentences.en: And at the same time, there are issues, like as you mentioned, with social media that are absolutely escalating this issue with boys and men.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，正如你所提到的，诸如社交媒体之类的问题绝对正在加剧男孩和男性的这一问题。

sentences.en: You and your colleagues coined the term muscle dysmorphia.
sentences.zh: 你和你的同事创造了“肌肉异形症”这个词。

sentences.en: What is muscle dysmorphia?
sentences.zh: 什么是肌肉异形症？

sentences.en: And how is it different from simply wanting to get stronger or more fit?
sentences.zh: 它与单纯想要变得更强壮或更健康有什么区别？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in research studies that I was doing at the time on eating disorders, I would get a lot of calls from men who said, well, I don't have an eating disorder, but I used to.
sentences.zh: 当时我在做关于饮食失调的研究时，会接到很多男性的电话，他们说，嗯，我没有饮食失调，但我以前有过。

sentences.en: I used to have, and many of them would say, I used to have anorexia nervosa.
sentences.zh: 很多人的说法是，我以前患有神经性厌食症。

sentences.en: And now they would say, I sort of have this other thing where the pendulum kind of swung in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们会说，我好像有了另一种情况，天平朝另一个方向倾斜了。

sentences.en: I'm still obsessed with food and with calories, except I'm eating food, but I'm obsessed with working out.
sentences.zh: 我仍然对食物和卡路里着迷，只不过我确实在吃东西，但我对锻炼着迷了。

sentences.en: So instead of wanting to be lean, I can't get big enough.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其说是想要保持苗条，不如说是我觉得自己的体型怎么也不够大。

sentences.en: I'm worried about losing size.
sentences.zh: 我担心体型变小。

sentences.en: And many of those men with anorexia said that they were never really seeking to be skinny or thin.
sentences.zh: 许多患有厌食症的男性表示，他们其实从来都不是为了追求骨感或纤瘦。

sentences.en: They were seeking to be lean, which is a little bit different in male body image than typically what you would see with female populations.
sentences.zh: 他们追求的是精瘦，这在男性身材认知上与女性群体中通常看到的情况略有不同。

sentences.en: So these were men who were, some of them had disordered eating or full-on clinical eating disorders.
sentences.zh: 所以这些男性中，有的人有饮食失调症，或者发展为完全的临床饮食失调症。

sentences.en: Some did not, but they were often muscular big guys who were obsessed with working out.
sentences.zh: 有的人则没有，但他们通常是那些沉迷于锻炼的肌肉健硕的大块头。

sentences.en: When they looked in the mirror, they saw someone who looked scrawny, weak, puny were the words that they would use.
sentences.zh: 当他们照镜子时，看到的是一个骨瘦如柴、虚弱、他们会用“瘦小”这个词来形容自己的人。

sentences.en: And despite people telling them, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 尽管人们对他们说，你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: You're a big guy, you're muscular, they didn't see it.
sentences.zh: 你是个大块头，你很有肌肉，但他们就是看不到。

sentences.en: And even if they saw it, the fear that tomorrow they could lose that drove them to compulsively work out at the gym.
sentences.zh: 而且即使他们看到了，那种明天可能会失去这一切的恐惧也会驱使他们在健身房里强迫性地锻炼。

sentences.en: Many of them were engaging in anabolic steroid use, engaging in a lot of harmful supplement use, avoiding situations.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有许多人开始使用合成代谢类固醇，使用大量有害的补剂，并且逃避社交场合。

sentences.en: And these are not men who are proudly showing off their physiques at Venice Beach, California.
sentences.zh: 这些可不是那些自豪地在加利福尼亚威尼斯海滩展示自己体魄的男性。

sentences.en: The men with muscle dysmorphia were, because they had this disordered body image, are covering their bodies up.
sentences.zh: 患有肌肉异形症的男性因为扭曲的身材认知，反而把自己的身体遮挡得严严实实。

sentences.en: They wouldn't leave the house because they felt that they looked too small.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不愿出门，因为他们觉得自己看起来太瘦小了。

sentences.en: So we first kind of coined reverse, is this reverse anorexia?
sentences.zh: 所以我们最初将其称为“反向神经性厌食症”吗？

sentences.en: And because it's not always an eating disorder, we really classified it as a subtype of body dysmorphic disorder.
sentences.zh: 由于它并不总是一种饮食失调，我们最终将其归类为身体变形障碍的一个亚型。

sentences.en: And that's where it sort of lies.
sentences.zh: 情况大致就是这样。

sentences.en: Are there triggers that essentially push men or boys into body dysmorphia or muscle dysmorphia?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么诱因会从根本上把男性或男孩推向身体变形障碍或肌肉异形症？

sentences.en: I've read that there's an association, for example, between having been bullied, but a lot of boys who are bullied don't end up with muscle dysmorphia.
sentences.zh: 我读到过，例如，曾遭受霸凌与此有关，但许多遭受霸凌的男孩最终并没有患上肌肉异形症。

sentences.en: So what do we know about its etiology?
sentences.zh: 那么我们对它的病因了解多少？

sentences.en: So if we look at this from various lenses, kind of in a biopsychosocial, social cultural model.
sentences.zh: 如果我们从不同的镜头来看待这个问题，也就是在生物-心理-社会-文化模型中来看。

sentences.en: So we do know that many of the boys and men with muscle dysmorphia do have for often family histories of depression, of obsessive compulsive disorder, of eating disorders.
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道，许多患有肌肉异形症的男孩和男性，通常都有抑郁症、强迫症或饮食失调的家族史。

sentences.en: Typically, psychologically, you'll often hear, I hear a lot in my patients, either histories of being bullied.
sentences.zh: 在心理层面上，你经常会听到，我在患者身上经常听到的是有遭受霸凌的历史。

sentences.en: And sometimes just unlike with girls with negative body image, you'll often find that girls who mature earlier are at higher risk of body image issues and receiving unwanted
sentences.zh: 有时不像对有负面身材认知的女孩那样，你经常会发现过早成熟的女孩面临更高身材焦虑的风险，并因其身体而受到不想要的

sentences.en: attention for their bodies.
sentences.zh: 关注。

sentences.en: With boys, it's the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但对于男孩来说，情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: The boys who mature later tend to be at higher risk.
sentences.zh: 较晚成熟的男孩往往面临更高的风险。

sentences.en: And when I say being bullied, particularly, I mean, sometimes for things that are unrelated
sentences.zh: 当我提到遭受霸凌时，特别是指有时是因为一些与外表无关的事情而遭到霸凌，

sentences.en: to appearance, but being bullied for appearance is not always being bullied for having a larger body, but actually being bullied for being too thin.
sentences.zh: 但因外表而遭霸凌并不总是因为身材较胖，实际上是因为长得太瘦而遭霸凌。

sentences.en: Because with male body image, being thin is associated with being, quote unquote, weak and not being masculine enough.
sentences.zh: 因为在男性的身材认知中，瘦弱与所谓的软弱以及缺乏男子气概联系在一起。

sentences.en: And so the idea of building this muscular body now became more than just, oh, I want to have this big body.
sentences.zh: 因此，打造肌肉发达体魄的想法，现在已经不仅仅是“哦，我想要有个大体格”那么简单了。

sentences.en: It's kind of this armor of masculinity and the symbol that that sort of represents.
sentences.zh: 它有点像男子气概的铠甲，也是这种象征意义的化身。

sentences.en: We also know, I see as far as comorbid or associated disorders, things like depression, social anxiety disorder is actually a very common one.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道，据我所知，就共病或相关障碍而言，像抑郁症、社交焦虑障碍其实是一种非常常见的病症。

sentences.en: And what I hear from a lot of my patients will say, you know, I feel so awkward in social
sentences.zh: 我的许多患者会告诉我，你知道，我在社交场合感到非常尴尬，

sentences.en: situations and particularly in dating kind of romantic relationships that if I just look a certain way, my body can sort of do the speaking for me, you know, in a way.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在约会这种恋爱关系中，如果我只要长成某种特定的样子，我的身体就能在某种程度上替我说话，你知道的。

sentences.en: And of course, we know that that doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们知道这根本行不通。

sentences.en: I mean, it might have people approach you, but then you still have to talk and converse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能会吸引别人接近你，但接下来你仍然必须开口说话和交流。

sentences.en: And then from a sociocultural manner that there's no question that, I mean, unlike with women
sentences.zh: 从社会文化的角度来看，毫无疑问，与历史上一直被灌输这种纤瘦审美意象的女性不同，

sentences.en: who historically have been promoted these sort of imagery, this imagery of thinness, I mean,
sentences.zh: 这种纤瘦的意象甚至可以追溯到 17 世纪，

sentences.en: going back to the 1600s, with boys and men, it's been a little bit different that in our research, we found that it was really the late 70s and early 80s where we really saw this
sentences.zh: 而对于男孩和男性来说情况则有些不同，我们的研究发现，真正看到这种对肌肉发达体型的

sentences.en: sort of promotion of muscular bodies.
sentences.zh: 大力推崇是在 20 世纪 70 年代末和 80 年代初。

sentences.en: I mean, if you think, you know, as a kid that grew up in the 80s, the biggest box office stars
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你回想一下，作为一个在 80 年代长大的孩子，票房大明星

sentences.en: were Sylvester Stallone and Arnold Schwarzenegger, who their bodies were like kind of a commodity
sentences.zh: 是西尔维斯特·史泰龙和阿诺德·施瓦辛格，他们的体魄就有点像是一种商品，

sentences.en: and Calvin Klein ads and sort of more sort of sort of men featured in advertisements with their chests and the fitness boom and bodybuilding kind of really kind of came into it.
sentences.zh: 还有卡尔文·克莱恩的广告，以及更多广告中展示胸肌的男性，再加上健身热潮和健美运动的兴起，真正推动了这一切。

sentences.en: Men's fitness and health magazines exploded.
sentences.zh: 男士健身与健康杂志如雨后春笋般涌现。

sentences.en: And I have to tell you, I mean, social media being doing this work, unlike any other condition
sentences.zh: 我必须告诉你，从事这项工作的我发现，与我接触过的任何其他病情诊断相比，

sentences.en: diagnosis that I work with, I have never seen something be so impacted by something on a sociocultural level as I have with the impact of social media on body image.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体对身材认知的影响之深，是我从未在社会文化层面上见过的。

sentences.en: I mean, it put gasoline on a fire with this issue.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它在这个问题上可谓火上浇油。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about that more, but I want to ask a question about how you know when
sentences.zh: 我们接下来会深入讨论这一点，但我想先问一个问题：你如何判断

sentences.en: somebody has crossed over from just wanting to be fit and looking good to having muscle dysmorphia.
sentences.zh: 某人是从“单纯想保持健康和外表好看”跨越到了患有“肌肉异形症”？

sentences.en: In other words, how do you diagnose this?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你该如何诊断这种疾病？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great question because this can be easily missed because unlike something like
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题，因为这很容易被忽视，因为不像厌食症那样，

sentences.en: anorexia, where sometimes it becomes more obvious when someone is malnourished and emaciated,
sentences.zh: 当一个人营养不良和骨瘦如柴时往往更加显眼，

sentences.en: we celebrate, you know, if you have a teenage boy that's going to the gym five days a week, it's like, great, he's not playing video games 14 hours a day and he's active.
sentences.zh: 如果一个十几岁的男孩一周去五天健身房，我们会庆祝，觉得太棒了，他没有一天玩 14 小时的电子游戏，而且他很活跃。

sentences.en: Um, I usually put it in these different categories.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我通常把它分为以下几个不同的类别。

sentences.en: One is, is there a presence of a body image distortion?
sentences.zh: 第一，是否存在身材认知扭曲？

sentences.en: So with people with muscle dysmorphia, they're not seeing themselves the way that other people are seeing them.
sentences.zh: 患有肌肉异形症的人，他们眼中的自己与其他人眼中的并不一样。

sentences.en: Um, there's a sort of like desperation that they feel around.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们周围弥漫着一种绝望感。

sentences.en: They're not just going to the gym because they enjoy it and, and, you know, they want to build their muscle and feel confident.
sentences.zh: 他们去健身房不仅仅是因为他们喜欢，而且，你知道，他们想锻炼肌肉并树立自信。

sentences.en: They feel like they have to.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己不得不去。

sentences.en: I mean, many of the men that I work with, with muscle dysmorphia, hate going to the gym.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我共事过的许多患有肌肉异形症的男性，其实讨厌去健身房。

sentences.en: They hate working out.
sentences.zh: 他们讨厌锻炼。

sentences.en: They feel imprisoned to it, like enslaved by it is how they sort of describe it.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己被其囚禁，就像被它奴役一样，他们经常这样描述。

sentences.en: But the feeling for them, if they don't do that can really plummet them sometimes into,
sentences.zh: 但对他们来说，如果不这样做，有时真的会让他们陷入

sentences.en: I mean, depressive, if not suicidal states, um, at times like the pandemic was, I mean, very, very hard for a lot of these people where gyms were closed.
sentences.zh: 抑郁甚至自杀的状态，有时像疫情期间，对许多这些人来说非常非常艰难，当时健身房都关门了，

sentences.en: And, and their acts accessibility to certain things.
sentences.zh: 他们获得某些事物的途径也受阻了。

sentences.en: So is there a body image distortion?
sentences.zh: 所以，是否存在身材认知扭曲？

sentences.en: And because if someone is starting from a place where they're not seeing themselves accurately, that's a red flag that there is good, a higher risk in terms of where they
